name: Diacerein

overview.mechanism: A medicine used for symptomatic treatment of osteoarthritis; safety restrictions are central to product selection.
uses: The EMA referral limits use to symptoms of hip or knee osteoarthritis.

paragraphs.text: The 2014 EU regulatory review restricted diacerein because of severe diarrhoea and liver injury. It is not recommended at age 65 years or older and must not be used with current or previous liver disease. Treatment should be initiated by a clinician experienced in osteoarthritis.

The EU restriction recommends starting at 50 mg daily for 2–4 weeks before 50 mg twice daily, stopping if diarrhoea develops, and monitoring for early liver problems. These are attributed EU instructions, not a verified Philippine regimen or a renal-dose adjustment.

Symptomatic benefit was first evident after 2–4 weeks in the studies reviewed by EMA. The referral does not provide an HD, PD or CRRT schedule; it should not be used as evidence for one. The EMA source is acknowledged for this regulatory summary.

sources.citation: European Medicines Agency. Restrictions to the use of diacerein-containing medicines. EMA/544268/2014, 4 September 2014.

draft_notes: International reference sources do not establish the current Philippine-approved product instructions. No unsupported dialysis regimen added.
